- Overestimate prices after strong sentiment spikes (especially sentiment > 0.7) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate when sentiment is negative or near-zero — model ignores downside risk, leading to lagged corrections.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after recent peaks, especially when sentiment is high and volatile.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts, underestimating sustained trends or overestimating volatility.
- When sentiment is consistently low or negative, model fails to adjust downward — true price often drops more sharply than forecasted.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves — model anticipates continuation, but sentiment often cools or reverses, causing overcorrection.
- Model underestimates downward momentum when sentiment is weak but price is trending up — fails to recognize “false breakout” scenarios.
- Sentiment-driven corrections are often delayed — model reacts to sentiment but doesn’t fully align with actual price behavior within 3–5 days.
